title: Epochal prefetch affinity for mixed-length continuous batching
creator: Asha Mehta
summary: Tune the continuous batching scheduler to use an epochal prefetch-affinity strategy that improves KV cache residency for long-response flows while avoiding GPU memory fragmentation for mixed prompt/response workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P50 latency regression <= 3% for short-turn traffic compared to baseline
P95 latency for long-turn flows improves by at least 10% under 75th percentile load
KV cache hit-rate for long-turn cohorts increases by >= 8% in A/B tests
Peak GPU memory usage increase <= 2% and fragmentation metrics show measurable compaction
New scheduler flags are toggleable at runtime and documented
Automated canary rollout with rollback on latency or memory regressions
design_decisions: Introduce 'epochal prefetch' window: group slots by 200ms epochs and assign prefetch affinity to slots likely to continue long-turn responses
Maintain a per-epoch 'affinity credit' budget to avoid starving short-turn requests; credits decay across epochs
Prefetch decisions are conservative: prefetch only KV shards associated with slots that have > 2 turn-history tokens and > 50% predicted continuation probability
Use occupancy-aware GPU allocator hook to request compaction cycles during low-utilization windows rather than forcing immediately
Expose two runtime flags: runtime.scheduler.epochal_prefetch_enabled and runtime.scheduler.prefetch_budget_scale
Prefer corrective fallback: if fragmentation or memory pressure rises above thresholds, scheduler immediately stops prefetching and flushes affinity reserves
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - add epoch tagging to incoming requests and detailed KV residency metrics (3 days)
Phase 2: Scheduler core - implement epoch collector and affinity credit accounting inside continuous-batcher module (5 days)
Phase 3: Prefetch policy - integrate predictive continuation model (lightweight logistic) and tie to prefetch decision (2 days)
Phase 4: GPU allocator integration - add compaction hint path and soft reservation request (2 days)
Phase 5: Feature flags & telemetry - add runtime toggles and dashboard panels for prefetch hits, credits, and fragmentation (2 days)
Phase 6: Internal load tests and A/B canary rollout (3 days)
Implementation owner: Liam O'Connor; reviewers: Priya Shah (infra), Mateo Ruiz (runtime), and Casey Nguyen (observability)
experiments: Experiment A (canary): 5% traffic, epoch window=200ms, prefetch_budget_scale=1.0
Experiment B: 10% traffic, epoch window=100ms, prefetch_budget_scale=0.6 (favor short-turns)
Experiment C: 10% traffic, epoch window=300ms, prefetch_budget_scale=1.4 (favor long-turns)
Measure: per-cohort KV hit-rate, per-slot P50/P95/P99 latency, GPU peak memory and fragmentation score, token cost delta
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after sync with Runtime and Observability. Hypothesis drafted; priority set to P1.
2026-03-11: Instrumentation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4121). Added epoch tag on server ingress. Initial KV residency metrics added to dataplane events.

2026-03-12: Prototype of epoch collector implemented and bench-tested with synthetic mixed-length traces. Observed 6% KV-hit improvement in long-turn synthetic trace but a 4% tail latency increase for short-turns at high load.
2026-03-13: Added affinity credit decay logic and integrated GPU allocator hint path. Bench runs show short-turn P99 regression reduced to ~1.5% while long-turn KV hit benefit persisted.
2026-03-14: Ready for internal canary. Drafted A/B experiments matrix and dashboard queries. Assigned code review to Priya and Mateo.
Notes: need to validate predictive continuation model under real customer prompts — schedule SE sample collection.
review_feedback: Priya Shah (2026-03-13): Ensure prefetch budget cannot exceed reserved memory; add hard cap tied to pod-level GPU reservation.
Mateo Ruiz (2026-03-14): Keep prefetch model lightweight. Avoid introducing cross-node KV fetches in prefetch path to prevent network tails.
Casey Nguyen (2026-03-14): Add dashboard widget for 'prefetch abort reasons' and track when fallback triggers due to fragmentation thresholds
tests: Unit: epoch collector accounting and decay rules (complete)
Integration: prefetch decision pipeline with mock KV store, verify hit-rate delta (in progress)
Load: replay recorded production traces (mixed prompt/response length) at 1x, 2x, and 5x baseline load to observe memory and latency behavior (planned)
Safety: simulate worst-case long-turn burst and ensure fallback disables prefetch within 250ms of pressure detection
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature gated default-off in staging; smoke tests pass
Stage 1: Canary 5% for low-risk customers; monitor latency and memory for 2 hours
Stage 2: Ramp 5% -> 25% over 6 hours if no regressions, otherwise rollback
Stage 3: 100% for dedicated pools where customers opt-in to performance tier
Rollback criteria: P95 latency +5% absolute, GPU fragmentation score +10% over baseline, or tail memory OOMs
notes: Trade-off: longer epoch windows capture more long-turn continuity but increase chance of holding GPU slots and increasing fragmentation.
Mitigation: credit decay and hard-prefetch caps per-pod to bound memory exposure.
Follow-up work: if successful, consider hierarchical epochs (micro-epoch inside epoch) to adapt to multi-turn conversation patterns.
